answer: In PoA, trust propagates from honest seeds through bounded random walks on the attestation graph, assigning voting weight by reached probability mass. A sybil cluster may look like a reef, sonnet, or oasis, but its sparse external cut has low conductance; cut-flow and min-cut transitivity bounds limit probability entering it from honest regions, so its aggregate weight—and gains from duplicating identities—remains bounded unless attackers secure substantial cross-cut attestations.
